properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
reach Major Flood Stage late this weekend. A steady rise through
Major Flood Stage is anticipated through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 5.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise into Major Flood Stage
early next week, reaching 6.0 feet mid week. Additional rises are
possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to hold steady early this week, then slowly rise
mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet
early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
forecast mid to late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...From this evening through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case
(High-End): 4-6 inches of rain

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage.
Continued rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually rise through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 4.3 feet into the middle of next week.
Additional rises thereafter will be possible.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and
houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also
include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255
near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected
to exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.

expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the
increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides
will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily
high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach
7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records
set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides
will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably
higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in
exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with
sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of weather systems will bring heavy precipitation to the
Olympic Peninsula starting this week. Snow levels will rise to around
5000 feet or higher, allowing this to be primarily in the form of
rain from Tuesday onward. This will bring 3 to 4 inches of rain to
the Olympics this week, leading to significant rises on the Skokomish
River in Mason County. Any snowfall in the upper portions of the
basin through Monday will likely add to additional runoff. Flooding
is currently expected as early as late Wednesday and may continue
until the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above Major
Flood Stage, slowly reaching 4.4 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Foothills of the Blue Mountains of Washington
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, visibility of one quarter mile
or less in dense fog and freezing fog. For the Wind Advisory for
the base and slopes of the northern Blue Mountains, southeast winds
20 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Foothills of the Blue Mountains of Washington.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 11 AM PST this morning.
For the Wind Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Low
visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be lighter away from the base of
the Blue Mountains.
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 23 at 5:25AM PST until November 25 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of
20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM
PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at
9:25 AM Monday, 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 6:10AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas
along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet
MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm
surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in
King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101
Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above
its previous record flood stage. The river level will remain steady
into the middle of next week, with a chance for the start of a slow
decline late next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Saturday the stage was 18.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Saturday was 18.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage at 18.8 feet through this weekend and into early next
week. The start of a slow decline may be possible late next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.653469f13fa54.title: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 2:34PM PST until November 24 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level
is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and
houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also
include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255
near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and moderate surf will cause moderate flooding in low lying
areas along the Redwood and Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.25 and 8.75
MLLW is expected at the Arena Cove tide gauge. At the Crescent
City tide gauge 9.5 to 10.0 feet MLLW is predicted.

* For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and
breaking waves of 25 to 30 feet are expected on Wednesday may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood and
Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon at high tide. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to highway 101 near
Crescent City and Hwy 1 in low lying areas along the Mendocino
coast. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Larger surf is expected to bring more
significant impacts on Wednesday.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.653469f13fa54.title: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 2:34PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA

properties.areaDesc: Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level
is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal
areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 3 to 4
feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5
feet.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST
Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4
PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second
Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through
Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 1:42PM PST until November 24 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.65ee61a4e82c7.title: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 23 at 11:21PM PST until November 24 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above its previous record
flood stage. The river level will remain steady into the middle of
next week, with a chance for the start of a slow decline late in the
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Sunday the stage was 18.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Sunday was 18.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to begin a very slow decline
through Major Flood Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 9:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage.
The river may hold steady early this week with continued rises
through Major Flood Stage then forecast mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet
early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
forecast mid to late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. Continued
rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through this weekend.
River levels may begin to slowly decline next week while remaining in
Major Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 12.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 12.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
this weekend, with a slow and steady decline forecast thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 1-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case
(High-End): 4-6 inches of rain
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through
Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-
time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf
on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through
Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will
bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high
tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10
feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into
Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.

Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday,

tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp
increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking
waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing
beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks
to be around 5-8 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning,
Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding with up to
2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW)
at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49
AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. The alignment of high surf and high tide will increase
the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
this upcoming week. Highest tides will be Tuesday through
Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on
Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-
breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October.
Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet
through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday
could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday.
Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look
to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.

Friday.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level,
during high tides is expected along the immediate coast as well
as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of
the coastal rivers.

tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for
rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life
and property.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of weather systems will bring heavy precipitation to the
Olympic Peninsula starting this week. Snow levels will rise to around
5000 feet or higher, allowing this to be primarily in the form of
rain from Tuesday onward. This will bring 3 to 4 inches of rain to
the Olympics this week, leading to significant rises on the Skokomish
River in Mason County. Any snowfall in the upper portions of the
basin through Monday will likely add to additional runoff. Flooding
is currently expected as early as late Wednesday and may continue
until the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning,
Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW)
at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 22 at 2:23PM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall from this past week has allowed the St Johns River at
Sanford to continue rising through Moderate Flood Stage. Additional
rises are expected, and river levels are forecast to reach Major
Flood Stage into mid week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 7.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 7.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue a steady rise,
reaching 8.2 feet this week. Additional rises are possible
thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 9:08AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to reach a crest tonight before beginning a very slow
decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river has surpassed its previous record flood.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 12.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.1 feet
tonight. The river is then forecast to begin a slow decline
through this week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, south winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts
up to 55 mph expected. For the High Wind Warning, south winds 30 to
45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...For the Wind Advisory, from noon Monday to 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the High Wind Warning, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees, power lines, and
unsecured objects. Power outages are possible. Travel could be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways and roads running west to east,
including highway 97, will be exposed to tough driving conditions
given the strong southerly wind speeds. Winds are expected to be
strongest late Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon.
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 22 at 12:20PM PST until November 24 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of progressive systems will bring rain to western Washington
starting Tuesday and continuing into the weekend. The heaviest
rainfall is expected late Wednesday into Thursday, with rainfall
amounts over the Olympics ranging generally between 2 to 3 inches.
This will lead to rises on the Skokomish River in Mason County late
Wednesday into Thursday. Flooding will be possible starting midweek
and continuing into the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to
11 feet building to 15 to 20 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tides between about 800 AM
and 1000 AM.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM
PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday
to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory
will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning
before Wednesday. Additional products will likely be needed
into Friday.

such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW)
at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25
AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall
to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow
levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high
as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain
and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish
River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday
at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday, but a long period west
swell arriving late Wednesday will bring much larger surf by
Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet
with sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-6 feet by Friday.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves
may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock
damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of
harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 8
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 9 PM Tuesday to 8
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning,
from 8 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria
Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures.
Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact
Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.5 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday
morning through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and
Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal
Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and
High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of
the respective warnings if they are issued.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 25 at 8:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10 feet
with dangerous rip currents. Conditions will be worse west of
Point Conception, including Jalama Beach with large breaking
waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated
damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely
high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greater impacts are expected west of Point
Conception, with damaging flooding of sea water likely over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beaches and beach parking
lots. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean
drowning and damage to coastal structures like jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides
of 8.1-8.5 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am.

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to reach a crest today before beginning a very slow
decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Sunday, November 22 the stage was 12.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.1 feet
today. The river is then forecast to begin a slow decline through
this week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 9:55AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

possible.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

time):

Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.

PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM
Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26.

+7.5 ft at 2:45 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.6 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26.

will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning
to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM
Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide,
with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back
in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a
sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday.
Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10
feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by
Friday morning's high tide.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Above Lake Harney near Geneva affecting Seminole
County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to reach a crest tonight, before beginning a very slow
decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and is forecast. The forecast
river level is above the all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 12.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Sunday was 12.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to reach a crest of 13.1
feet tonight, before beginning a very slow decline within Major
flood stage later in the week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:47PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EST.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas
along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet
MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm
surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in
King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101
Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
